JUDGMENT Claimant in MVC No.330/2003 has sought for enhanced compensation by challenging the judgment and award passed in MVC No.330/2003 on the file of Additional Civil Judge (Sr. Dn.) and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ranebennur, dated 04.12.2009.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ranebennur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Facts in brief which are not in dispute are as under:
2.1. Claimant is the dependant of rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-17/Q-7961 who lost his life in a road traffic accident that occurred on 16.02.2003 at about 3.00 p.m.
3.
Tribunal has allowed the claim petition on contest in a sum of Rs.4,33,000/-.
4. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and award, claimant is in appeal.

5. Reiterating the grounds urged in the appeal memorandum, Shri. S. N. Banakar, learned counsel for the appellant sought for enhanced compensation following the NC: 2024:KHC-D:3709 dictum of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in AIR 2017 SCC 5157, in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram and Others reported in 2018 ACJ 2782 and in the case of United India Insurance Company Limited vs. Satinder Kaur alias Satwinder Kaur and Others reported in AIR 2020 SC 3076.
6.

sentences.text: Per contra, Shri. G. N. Raichur, learned counsel for respondent No.1 supported the impugned judgment and sought for dismissal of the appeal.

sentences.text: 7. Having heard the parties in detail about the merits of the matter, this Court perused the material on record meticulously.
8. On such perusal, it is noticed that the appeal filed by the Insurance Company challenging the judgment and award came to be dismissed on the ground of delay.

9. There is a scope for re-assessment of the compensation Following the dictum of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the cases of Pranay Sethi, Magma General Insurance Company Limited and Satinder Kaur (supra), which is re- assessed as under:
NC: 2024:KHC-D:3709 1 Loss of dependency Rs.4,64,100/-
Rs.3,250 + 40% (i.e.,Rs.1300/-) = Rs.4,550 / 2 = Rs.2,275/-
(2275 x 12 x 17) 2 Loss of parental consortium Rs.80,000/- 3 Loss of estate Rs.15,000/-
4 Loss of funeral expenses Rs.15,000/-
Total Rs.5,74,100/-
10.

Accordingly, the following order is passed:
ORDER i).
Appeal is allowed in part.

ii). As against the sum of Rs.4,33,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal, the claimant is entitled to a sum of Rs.5,74,100/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
iii). Insurance Company is granted four weeks time to pay the balance amount.

Sd/-
